newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela still confident about peace in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Mandela still confident about peace in Zaire.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela said on Tuesday he was in regular contact with Zaire's warring leaders and remained confident of making progress towards a peace deal when they meet for the second time on Wednesday.
"I am very confident that we will make progress...as long as everybody understands that this is not an event, it is a process," Mandela told reporters in Cape Town.

Mandela said he had spoken regularly in the past few days to Zairean President Mobuto Seso Seko, to rebel leader Laurent Kabila and to the leaders of countries such as Upper Volta, Togo and Nigeria in a bid to map out a settlement.
An aide said earlier Mandela had also telephoned the presidents of Zimbabwe, Tanzania, Congo and Gabon.
Mandela is scheduled to chair the second direct meeting between Mobutu and Kabila aboard the South African ice-breaker Outeniqua in or near the Congolese port of Pointe Noire on Wednesday.
He said the meeting was on, but warned that peace was not an overnight event and would take time to resolve.
"You don't expect to deal with a situation such as exists in Zaire, to achieve peace in a short period of time. It is a process, and we approach it from that angle," he said.

Mandela said South Africa did not regard itself as the regional problem solver, but was willing to work with the Southern African Development Community, the Organisation of African Unity and the United Nations to resolve regional conflicts.
Mandela spoke to reporters while appearing for photographers with visiting Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari, who praised his Zairean peace initiative.

"It requires enormous courage to try to facilitate a peaceful change...it is never easy. There are always people who want to criticise...but it requires special courage to try to facilitate, to bring the people together."
